value.body: A metallurgical engineer makes sure metals come out with the right composition, structure and properties — in a steel plant, an aluminium or copper smelter, a foundry, a forging shop or a heat-treatment line. Steel and non-ferrous producers, foundries, forging and automotive component makers hire them. A day involves checking process data and test results, solving defects, and adjusting process settings with the production team.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Tech / B.E. in Metallurgical or Materials Engineering

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Spectrometer, optical microscope, hardness and tensile testers

items.label: Work pattern
items.value: Plant-based; shift duty is common at entry

items.label: Crude steel production
items.note: Up from ~144 million tonnes in FY2023-24
items.source: Ministry of Steel Annual Report 2025-26 (JPC data)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually join as graduate or management trainees through campus placement at steel, non-ferrous and component companies. Steel and mineral PSUs recruit through GATE (Metallurgical paper) or their own exams, followed by interviews.

value.title: At a glance
items: Large plants are often in mineral belts and industrial towns.
Common next roles: senior metallurgist, process or quality head, R&D or product development.
Research and advanced-materials roles often expect an M.Tech or PhD.
